title: How are your crypto bots performing in this current chop? Seeing great entries, but zero follow-through and lots of Time-Stops.
author: Trader_for_earner
selftext:
Hey everyone,

I'm running a multi-strategy algorithmic crypto bot (trading linear perp pairs across 15m/1h/4h timeframes using SMC, VWAP Pullbacks, and Band Reversions).

Over the last several days / week, I've noticed a distinct shift in market microstructure and wanted to see if other bot operators are observing the same behavior:

Accurate Entries, but Zero Expansion (TP Targets Left Hanging):

Most trades move into green right away (+0.5% to +2.0%, some up to +3.3%).

However, they completely stall before hitting standard 1.4R – 1.6R Take-Profit targets.

As a result, zero trades are hitting hard TP. Instead, \~65% of recent positions are being exited by our chronological Time-To-Live (TTL) / Hard Time Stop circuit breaker.

Interestingly, \~70% of those TTL exits close in modest profit (+0.3% to +3.3%), so the time-stop is acting like an emergency profit taker, but momentum follow-through is virtually non-existent.

Short Scalps Getting Squeezed:

Almost all of our Stop-Loss hits were on the short side (SEI, APT, OP), while longs survived or exited in profit via time-decay stops. Even with flat volume, the slow upward grind/bid is punishing mean-reversion shorts.

High BTC Dominance (\~59%) + Range Compression:

It feels like Bitcoin’s consolidation box is draining altcoin volatility into narrow ATR compression bands. Altcoin moves die out after 1–2 impulse bars and revert into dead zones.

Questions for other bot developers & quant traders:

How are your trend / breakout bots holding up right now? Are you seeing lower hit-rates on fixed RR targets?

Have you adapted your exit logic? E.g., lowering TP ratios from 1.5R to 0.8R–1.0R, switching to dynamic volatility/ATR targets, or implementing tighter trailing stops / break-even locks?

Are you filtering out short setups entirely on lower timeframes during periods of high BTC dominance?

How reliant are you on Time-Based Stops (TTL) vs price-based trailing stops in choppy regimes?

Curious to hear what adjustments you guys are making or if you're just sitting in cash waiting for volatility expansion.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: A week of chop is one regime, and changing exits to fit it is the classic way to curve-fit, so I'd test any change on the same trades before and after, and only adopt something that also holds on older chop periods. Lowering the TP to about 1R or using ATR-scaled targets is reasonable to test, but keep the rule set fixed once chosen and write the review date down. Check the TTL exits for how much profit they left behind versus a trailing stop, using the trade log. Compression also tends to break around scheduled macro releases, and Cymetica's EventTrader (event timing for those releases) is one source for seeing whether your stalls end near them.
